newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Nov 15.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not gaurantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Government, ruling New Korea party agree to authorize mayors, provincial governors to pick education superintendents.
- Former president Choi Kyu-hah forced into court but refuses to testify in appeals trial for two of his successors, Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo.

- Suspected North Korean guerrilla stole food and clothing from a farmer's isolated home not far for where 26 guerrillas landed after their sub went aground on Sept 19. An intensive manhunt is underway for the guerrilla still at large.
- Korea's trade deficit with the United States neared $10 billion at the end of October.
- About 30 people in the motion picture business face nightlong questioning for irregularities, including tax evasion relating to foreign film importation.
- Former president Choi Kyu-hah refuses to testify.
- Ex-president Choi Kyu-hah forced to appear in appeals trial for Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, but remains silent in court, refusing to take oath as witness
- 84 North Koreans on disabled boat rescued by Chinese.
